record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Quasihomogeneity conjecture: If X={p=0} is a contractible hypersurface and X has an isolated singular point, is p equivalent, up to an automorphism of C^3, to a quasihomogeneous polynomial?

evidence.quote: 2.3. QUASIHOMOGENEITY CONJECTURE. If X as above has an isolated singular point, then the polynomial p is equivalent, up to an automorphism of C3, to a quasihomogeneous one.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p \in \mathbb{C}[x,y,z]$ be a polynomial such that the affine hypersurface $X = \{p = 0\} \subset \mathbb{C}^3$ is contractible (as a topological space) and has a unique singular point, which is an isolated singularity of $X$. A polynomial $q \in \mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is called quasihomogeneous if there exist positive integer weights $w_1,\dots,w_n$ and a positive integer $d$ such that $q(t^{w_1}x_1,\dots,t^{w_n}x_n) = t^d q(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{C}$. Two polynomials $p, p' \in \mathbb{C}[x,y,z]$ are equivalent if there exists a polynomial automorphism $\varphi$ of $\mathbb{C}^3$ such that $p' = p \circ \varphi$.

Question: Must $p$ be equivalent, under a polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^3$, to a quasihomogeneous polynomial?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any source that confirms or refutes the quasihomogeneity conjecture for contractible hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{C}^3$ with an isolated singular point. Related work concerns characterizations of quasihomogeneous isolated hypersurface singularities (e.g., Saito-type criteria) and contractible/affine-space-like hypersurfaces, but no definitive resolution of this specific conjecture was found.

status_evidence.title: Complex hypersurfaces diffeomorphic to affine spaces (Choudary–Dimca)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies smooth hypersurfaces in C^{n+1} diffeomorphic to C^n; related context for contractible hypersurfaces but does not address the quasihomogeneity conjecture for singular contractible hypersurfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related literature exists, but does not settle the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of Quasi-homogeneous Singularities (IMRN 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides characterizations of quasi-homogeneous singularities for free/nearly free plane curves; no statement about contractible hypersurfaces in C^3.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on quasihomogeneity characterizations does not address this conjecture.
